summary: Phase 3 of a 6-phase procurement spend cube system. Builds the hybrid spend categorisation pipeline: 6-pass system running in strict order of confidence. Pass 1: deterministic GL mapping. Pass 2: deterministic supplier mapping. Pass 3: keyword/rule-based matching. Pass 4: embedding similarity (sentence-transformers). Pass 5: LLM fallback (Claude API, batched, dry-run aware). Pass 6: human review queue. Also loads UNSPSC reference hierarchy and internal category hierarchy, builds category_overrides feedback table, and wires everything into the categoriser orchestrator. Validation gate: 80%+ of sample data categorised at HIGH or MEDIUM confidence. 12+ passing unit tests.

decisions.pass_order: 6 passes in strict order. Each pass only runs on items not yet classified above confidence threshold. Stops as soon as confidence >= 0.60 (MEDIUM). Items below 0.60 after all passes go to review queue.
decisions.confidence_cap_llm: LLM results always capped at 0.70 confidence regardless of model output — per spec.
decisions.internal_category_hierarchy: 3-level internal taxonomy (L1/L2/L3) stored in data/reference/internal_category_hierarchy.csv. Created in this sprint. Maps to UNSPSC segments. L1 examples: IT, Facilities, Logistics, Office Supplies, Marketing, HR, Finance, Professional Services.
decisions.category_seed_mappings: data/reference/category_seed_mappings.csv already exists from Phase 1 (200+ rows with SUPPLIER, GL, KEYWORD mapping_type). Phase 3 uses this as starting point for passes 1-3.
decisions.unspsc_loader: data/reference/unspsc_v24.csv already exists from Phase 1. Phase 3 loads it and builds category description embeddings for Pass 4.
decisions.keyword_rules_yaml: Keyword rules stored in data/reference/keyword_rules.yaml (created this sprint) — configurable outside code. Each rule: pattern (regex), l1, l2, l3, unspsc_segment_code, confidence.
decisions.category_overrides: category_overrides_table already defined in src/models/database.py (Phase 1). Phase 3 reads from it as the highest-priority override (effectively Pass 0).
decisions.embedding_cache: Category description embeddings cached to data/cache/category_embeddings.pkl — same pattern as Phase 2 supplier embeddings.
decisions.idempotency: Running categoriser twice on same transactions: skips rows already classified at >= MEDIUM confidence unless --force flag passed.
decisions.phase_foundation: Phases 1 and 2 are complete. transactions table populated with canonical supplier IDs. src/models/schema.py has CategoryMethod enum. config.yaml has categorisation thresholds.

existing_tables.transactions: All canonical fields including category columns (unspsc_segment/family/class/commodity, internal_category_l1/l2/l3, category_confidence, category_method) — these get populated by the categoriser. Also has canonical_supplier_id from Phase 2.
existing_tables.category_overrides: id, canonical_supplier_id, gl_account, override_l1, override_l2, override_l3, unspsc_code, reviewer, reason, created_at — defined in src/models/database.py, read as Pass 0 override

key_files: src/models/schema.py - CategoryMethod enum (DETERMINISTIC_GL, DETERMINISTIC_SUPPLIER, KEYWORD, EMBEDDING, LLM, MANUAL), ConfidenceBand (Phase 1)
src/config.py - load_config() with categorisation section: confidence_high=0.85, confidence_medium=0.60, embedding_threshold=0.80, llm_fallback_threshold=0.60 (Phase 1)
patterns_to_follow: Each module independently runnable via CLI — same pattern as Phase 1/2
Each pass returns (classified_df, unclassified_df) — unclassified passed to next pass
category_method field always set to the CategoryMethod enum value that produced the classification
All LLM calls batched (config.llm.batch_size=20), logged via log_llm_call(), skip when dry_run=true
confidence_high=0.85, confidence_medium=0.60 from config — items below 0.60 after all passes → review queue
UNSPSC codes stored at segment level minimum; commodity level preferred when deterministic match available

userStories.title: Implement deterministic GL and supplier categorisation
userStories.description: Implement src/categorisation/deterministic.py with two deterministic passes: Pass 1 (GL code mapping) and Pass 2 (supplier mapping). Both use data/reference/category_seed_mappings.csv as lookup. Also implements Pass 0: category_overrides table lookup (highest priority, always checked first).
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/categorisation/deterministic.py — implement DeterministicCategoriser class
__init__(self, seed_mappings_path: str, engine, config): loads category_seed_mappings.csv, loads category_overrides from DB via pd.read_sql, loads internal_category_hierarchy.csv for UNSPSC lookup

Implement apply_overrides(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: Pass 0. Checks category_overrides table — matches on canonical_supplier_id OR gl_account. Returns (classified_df with category fields populated, unclassified_df). Confidence=1.0, method='MANUAL'.

Implement apply_gl_mapping(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: Pass 1. For each row, look up gl_account in seed_mappings where mapping_type='GL'. Match on exact GL code first, then on GL prefix (first 4 digits). Assign confidence from seed mapping row. Returns (classified, unclassified).

Implement apply_supplier_mapping(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: Pass 2. For each row, look up canonical_supplier_name in seed_mappings where mapping_type='SUPPLIER' (case-insensitive). Assign confidence from seed mapping row. Returns (classified, unclassified).
Each classified row gets: internal_category_l1, internal_category_l2, internal_category_l3, unspsc_segment (from hierarchy lookup), category_confidence, category_method set appropriately.
GL prefix matching: normalise GL codes by stripping leading zeros, try exact match then try first-4-digits prefix (e.g. gl_account='6420100' → try '6420100' then '6420').
CLI: python src/categorisation/deterministic.py — loads sample transactions, runs all 3 passes, prints classification counts per pass and method

userStories.title: Implement keyword rule-based categorisation
userStories.description: Implement Pass 3 of the categorisation pipeline in src/categorisation/deterministic.py (extending the existing class): keyword/regex rule matching against cleaned_description and raw_line_description. Rules loaded from data/reference/keyword_rules.yaml.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/categorisation/deterministic.py — add apply_keyword_rules(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame] method to DeterministicCategoriser
Load keyword_rules.yaml in __init__ (already has path from config). Store as list of compiled regex patterns with associated category fields.

For each unclassified row: apply each rule's pattern against the combined text of cleaned_description + ' ' + raw_line_description (lowercased). Use re.search (not match). First rule that matches wins.
Assign: internal_category_l1/l2/l3 from rule, unspsc_segment from rule, category_confidence from rule's confidence value, category_method='KEYWORD'.
If multiple rules match, use the highest-confidence rule.

Verify against sample data: 'Office supplies - toner cartridges HP' row should match toner/cartridge rule → Office Supplies/Print Consumables, 'Catering - Q1 events' → Facilities/Catering, 'Staff canteen March' → Facilities/Catering, 'International freight - Shanghai to Melb' → Logistics/Freight, 'Mobile fleet - Feb 2024 (450 handsets)' → IT/Telecoms, 'Ad hoc signage for conference' → Marketing/Print
CLI: python src/categorisation/deterministic.py — after adding keyword pass, verify 6 of the 10 sample rows are classified by passes 1-3 combined

userStories.title: Implement embedding-based category classifier
userStories.description: Implement src/categorisation/embedding_classifier.py as Pass 4: encode transaction descriptions with sentence-transformers and compare against category description embeddings. Only invoked for transactions not classified by passes 1-3.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/categorisation/embedding_classifier.py — implement EmbeddingCategoriser class

__init__(self, hierarchy_path: str, model_name: str = 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2', cache_path: str = 'data/cache/category_embeddings.pkl', config=None): loads internal_category_hierarchy.csv, builds category descriptions by concatenating l1_name + ' ' + l2_name + ' ' + l3_name for each unique L2. Loads or computes embeddings for all category descriptions, caches to data/cache/category_embeddings.pkl.

Implement classify(self, description: str, config) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None, str | None, float, str, str]: encodes description, computes cosine similarity against all category embeddings. Returns (l1, l2, l3, unspsc_segment, confidence, method, evidence). If top similarity >= config.categorisation.embedding_threshold (0.80): confidence = top_similarity * 0.9, method='EMBEDDING'. If top-2 similarities within 0.05 of each other AND both above 0.70: flag as ambiguous → confidence = top_similarity * 0.75 (pushes toward review queue). Below threshold → (None, None, None, None, top_similarity, 'EMBEDDING_REJECT', evidence).

Implement classify_batch(self, df: pd.DataFrame, config) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: batch version. Returns (classified_df, unclassified_df) where unclassified = rows where confidence < config.categorisation.confidence_medium.
evidence string: f'cosine={top_similarity:.3f} top_category={best_category} second={second_similarity:.3f}'
If sentence-transformers unavailable: log warning, return all rows as unclassified (pass-through to LLM)
CLI: python src/categorisation/embedding_classifier.py — encodes sample descriptions, prints top-3 category matches with similarity scores for each

userStories.title: Implement LLM fallback categoriser
userStories.description: Implement src/categorisation/llm_classifier.py as Pass 5: Claude API batched classification for transactions still unclassified after passes 1-4. Must respect dry_run, batch 20 items per call, cap confidence at 0.70, and log all calls for auditability.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/categorisation/llm_classifier.py — implement LLMCategoriser class

__init__(self, config, hierarchy_path: str): loads config, loads internal_category_hierarchy.csv to build valid category list string for prompt context. Initialises anthropic.Anthropic() client only if not dry_run.

Implement classify_batch(self, items: list[dict], config) -> list[dict]: if dry_run, return list of dicts with all category fields None, confidence=0.0, method='DRY_RUN' for each item. Each item dict has keys: transaction_id, description, supplier_name, gl_account.
Use model=config.llm.model, max_tokens=2000, temperature=0.
Parse JSON response. Cap all confidence values at 0.70. Set method='LLM'. Handle malformed JSON gracefully (log error, skip batch items).
Log every call via log_llm_call() from src/utils/logging.py with prompt, response, model.

Implement classify_dataframe(self, df: pd.DataFrame, config) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: wraps classify_batch for DataFrame input. Returns (classified_df, unclassified_df) — unclassified = items where LLM returned None or confidence=0.
CLI: python src/categorisation/llm_classifier.py — with dry_run=true, prints 'DRY RUN' and sample items that would be sent to LLM

userStories.title: Implement categoriser orchestrator
userStories.description: Implement src/categorisation/categoriser.py as the main orchestrator that runs all 6 passes in strict order, produces the review queue, and updates the transactions table with category assignments. This is the main entry point for the categorisation phase.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/categorisation/categoriser.py — implement SpendCategoriser class
__init__(self, config, engine): initialises DeterministicCategoriser, EmbeddingCategoriser, LLMCategoriser

Implement categorise(self, transactions_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: runs passes in strict order. Pass 0: overrides. Pass 1: GL mapping. Pass 2: supplier mapping. Pass 3: keyword rules. Pass 4: embedding classifier. Pass 5: LLM (only items still below llm_fallback_threshold=0.60 after pass 4). After all passes: any remaining unclassified rows get category_confidence=0.0, category_method=None. Returns full transactions_df with all category fields populated.

Implement get_review_queue(self, transactions_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: returns rows where category_confidence < config.categorisation.confidence_medium (0.60), sorted by abs(base_amount) descending (highest spend reviewed first).

Implement update_transactions_in_db(self, transactions_df: pd.DataFrame, engine) -> int: updates transactions table rows with new category fields (UPDATE WHERE transaction_id=?). Returns count of rows updated.

Implement apply_feedback(self, overrides: list[dict], engine) -> None: inserts new rows into category_overrides_table. Each override: canonical_supplier_id or gl_account, l1/l2/l3, unspsc_code, reviewer, reason.
Log pass-by-pass summary: e.g. 'Pass 1 (GL): 2 classified, 8 remaining. Pass 2 (Supplier): 1 classified, 7 remaining...'

CLI: python src/categorisation/categoriser.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db: loads transactions, runs full categorisation, prints: total rows, classified by pass breakdown, review queue size, % at HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW confidence

risks: GL prefix matching edge cases: some GL codes have leading zeros stripped (Phase 1 handles normalisation). DeterministicCategoriser must normalise GL codes consistently before lookup — strip non-numeric, do not zero-pad.
Keyword rule order matters: more specific rules should be checked before generic ones. YAML rules loaded in order — document that specificity ordering is important.
Embedding model cold start: first run downloads all-MiniLM-L6-v2 if not cached. Same model as Phase 2 — likely already downloaded.
Intercompany and tax rows: these are legitimately hard to categorise into procurement categories. Acceptable for them to land in review queue — they should be flagged as non-addressable spend anyway.

80% threshold with 10-row sample: 8/10 rows must reach MEDIUM+ confidence. TAX-ADJ-001 (GST line) and INTERCOMPANY - LEGAL are the expected review queue candidates — both have is_tax_line/is_intercompany flags set from Phase 1.
